answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identities to proof of physical location via radio trilateration. Agents compute propagation delays against a synchronized timing pulse from anchor beacons. An adversary must provision distinct transceivers across separated sites, whether near a coastal reef or an open dune, incurring real hardware and real-estate costs per identity. However, this design is limited by multipath interference, which distorts timing and triggers false rejections.
